title: Macedonian — official 2008 system (passports, ID cards, driving licences; = ICAO Doc 9303)
authority: Government of North Macedonia, system for official documents adopted in 2008, based on ICAO Doc 9303 Part 3 §6.B Macedonian exceptions
description: Diacritic-free digraph system printed in North Macedonian passports, ID cards and driving licences since 2008: Ѓ→Gj, Ж→Zh, Ѕ→Dz, Ј→J, Љ→Lj, Њ→Nj, Ќ→Kj, Х→H, Ц→C, Ч→Ch, Џ→Dj, Ш→Sh. The upper-case output is also the MRZ string.
notes: The legal instrument (number and date of the 2008 decision) was not verified in a North Macedonian primary source; the table is attested by Wikipedia and agrees with the ICAO §6.B Macedonian exceptions.
ICAO §6.B prints the Macedonian GJ exception under U+0492 (Ғ) instead of U+0403 (Ѓ) and omits Ѓ; this scheme uses Ѓ→GJ as intended.

Collision: DJ here means Џ, whereas in Serbian/Croatian English convention dj means Ђ/Đ; DZ here means Ѕ, whereas in Serbian ICAO output it means Џ. Cross-language reverse mapping must be language-tagged.
Not reversible: zh/sh/ch/dz/gj/kj also arise from з+х, с+х, ц+х, д+з, г+ј, к+ј.
Older or alternative spellings to accept when matching: Ѓ as G, Đ, Dj; Ќ as K, Ć, Ch; Џ as Dž, Dzh; Ж as Ž, J; Ц as Ts.
The modifier apostrophe ʼ (U+02BC, e.g. ʼРжаново) becomes an ASCII apostrophe; ICAO omits it in the MRZ. Accented ѐ/ѝ → e/i; combining stress marks are deleted by aliases.
